text:
maria_support: Heads-up — customer ACME GmbH (DE) reporting intermittent 500ms+ p95 and sporadic 401s this morning. They say it only happens during traffic spikes.

jon_eng-runtime: Seen this before — usually fallback path is choosing us-east when eu pool is saturated. Any logs?

maria_support: Pasted what they grabbed from their app (redacted):
```
Request: POST /v1/generate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer ***  X-Region-Hint: eu-west-1
Response: 200 (tok 15ms) / 401 (after 220ms) / 200
Response-Headers when 401: X-Upstream-Region: us-east-1  X-Route-Policy: fallback
```
They also attached a HAR with slow DNS -> but our front door shows eu LB accepted connection then proxied to us-east.

lee_sre: @jon can you pull edge-proxy logs for that org id? I want to see routing decision + health checks around the spike window (09:12-09:30 CET).

jon_eng-runtime: grabbing... attaching snippet: 
```
[09:15:03] route_decision: org=acme id=org-789 hint=eu-west-1 candidate_pools=[eu-west-1, eu-central-1] selected_pool=eu-west-1
[09:15:03] upstream_resolve: eu-west-1 -> 10.12.8.3 (ok)
[09:15:03] proxy_request: chosen_instance=eu-west-1-3 latency_est=40ms
[09:15:03.220] fallback: reason=pool_congestion fallback_pool=us-east-1 selected_by=route-fallback
[09:15:03.221] auth: upstream=us-east-1 returned=401 token-check=failed (service-account-mismatch)
```
Looks like fallback happened inside route policy when queue depth breached threshold. When fallback hits a different region we saw token validation fail because service-account keys are region-scoped for some private deployments.

olivia_prod: Confirmed: a handful of dedicated customers use region-scoped service accounts for host-metadata. When traffic is routed cross-region, authz can fail with 401. That's likely why the customer saw auth errors during failover. Also billing: crossing region egress triggered unexpected charges per their report.

maria_support: Customer asked for a quick mitigation: keep them pinned to eu-west-1 until we patch auth fallback behavior. Can we do a temp sticky pin for org-789?

jon_eng-runtime: Short-term we can add an entry in the route sticky table: 
```
PATCH /admin/route-sticky/org-789 {preferred_region: eu-west-1, ttl: 72h}
```
But need SRE approval for manual sticky overrides. Also this only prevents fallback during saturation — doesn't fix underlying congestion.

lee_sre: +1 for manual sticky if customer impact high. Also want to adjust fallback policy to prefer local replica with degraded QoS instead of full cross-region fallback (we already have config flags: fallback.mode and fallback.auth_check). I can flip fallback.auth_check=false for the 1h window as emergency — that will allow fallback without auth mismatch checks but could expose tokens to wrong region (low risk for this customer?).

carmen_account: Customer is on a reserved capacity plan but with bursts allowed. They're upset about latency and the unexpected cross-region billing. They want an ETA for the fix and the sticky pin ASAP.

raj_support: I'll message them and request permission for sticky pin + auth_check toggle. If they approve I can schedule the change.

deploy-bot: Staging rollout: routing-policy-v2 -> canary completed 2026-03-17T09:00:00Z :rocket:

jon_eng-runtime: Note — routing-policy-v2 introduced a prefetch heuristic that aggressively moves traffic when queue_len > 80% to avoid tail latency. That heuristic didn't consider region-scoped auth tokens. We need two things: 1) quick guardrail to prevent cross-region fallback for orgs flagged with region-scoped credentials, 2) long term: have fallback do auth token translation/reauth.

lee_sre: Proposed immediate plan: 1) Put sticky pin for org-789 to eu-west-1 (72h) 2) Temporarily set fallback.auth_check=false for acme customer (1h) while we drain pressure, 3) Open ticket to change routing heuristic to check org metadata before cross-region fallback.

jon_eng-runtime: I'll open PR to add org metadata check to the decision path and write unit tests. Link: https://git.redwood/inference/routing/pulls/987 (WIP).

olivia_prod: Ops notes: Need comms template for billing — alert finance and customer success to prepare refund/credit if charges > X threshold. Carmen please coordinate.

carmen_account: On it. Also asking legal whether toggling fallback.auth_check for a customer needs additional approvals.

maria_support: Customer approved sticky pin and temporary toggle. Raj please schedule the changes and confirm once done.

raj_support: Doing now. Will report back when both are applied and we validate with the customer. ETA ~ 15m.

(15m later)
raj_support: Done — sticky applied and fallback.auth_check=false for org-789 for 1h. Customer observed p95 drop from ~620ms -> ~85ms and no 401s in the last 10 mins. They confirmed reduced errors. :thumbsup:

lee_sre: Follow-ups: we need a regression test that simulates a cross-region fallback with region-scoped tokens and asserts no 401s (or that fallback is disallowed). I'll add it to the incident ticket.

jon_eng-runtime: Agreed. Also schedule a config audit to find other orgs with region-scoped credentials and either auto-pin them or treat them as non-fallback eligible.

maria_support: Closing loop with customer now. Filing postmortem once PR merges. Thanks all.

— end of thread —
